title: Andhra Earmarks 5,000 Acres Near Tirupati for Space Sector Push
excerpt: At the CII Partnership Summit's close, Naidu named the Tirupati land bank as rocket startups Agnikul Cosmos and Hathor Rockets signed MoUs worth a proposed Rs 760 crore combined.
body:
• Andhra Pradesh has earmarked 5,000 acres near Tirupati for the space sector, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said on the closing day of the CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam.
  • Two space startups signed MoUs at the summit: Agnikul Cosmos (proposed Rs 510 crore, 350 jobs) and Hathor Rockets (Rs 250 crore, 200 jobs), both in aerospace and defence.
  • In all, 11 MoUs worth a proposed Rs 1,40,705 crore, with an estimated 10,472 jobs, were signed on November 13 in the Chief Minister's presence.
  • MoUs are proposals, not grounded projects — Naidu himself urged companies to focus on implementation, not just signatures.

Andhra Pradesh's pitch to become a space-manufacturing state got its land bank this week. On the second and concluding day of the 31st CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam on November 13, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said the state government had earmarked 5,000 acres near Tirupati for the space sector, adding that the region was well suited to space and defence industries, Rights Media reported. The announcement was the summit's headline version of a plan the state has been building under its Space Policy 4.0: dedicated space cities at Lepakshi and Tirupati, with a state target of Rs 25,000 crore in space-sector investment.

Two rocket startups sign on

Among the 11 MoUs signed on the closing day, two were space companies. Agnikul Cosmos Private Limited signed for a proposed investment of Rs 510 crore in aerospace and defence, generating an estimated 350 jobs. Hathor Rockets Private Limited signed for Rs 250 crore, with an estimated 200 jobs. The day's full list totalled a proposed Rs 1,40,705 crore with employment potential of 10,472 jobs, and included JSW Steel (Rs 15,000 crore, 2,500 jobs), Indian Oil in renewable energy (Rs 6,600 crore, 800 jobs) and Kakinada Seaports (Rs 6,452 crore, 852 jobs), plus a government order for Hindalco's expansion (Rs 880 crore, 447 jobs). All of these figures are the companies' proposals as announced at the summit, not completed investments.

Why Tirupati

Tirupati's case is geography. The district sits within reach of Sriharikota, India's orbital launch site, and the state has previously described a Tirupati Space City focused on launch-vehicle assembly, satellite and payload assembly, and electronics and avionics manufacturing, with a Lepakshi facility focused on design and development. At the summit's inaugural session a day earlier, the Chief Minister had set a separate Rs 25,000 crore target for the space sector within a Rs 50,000 crore aerospace and defence target, and said road connectivity from the Tirupati cluster to Sriharikota was part of the plan.

The implementation test

Naidu used the closing session to press the point that signatures are the easy part. He called on industrialists to focus not only on signing agreements but on grounding projects and ensuring timely implementation, and assured state support in taking projects forward. That caution applies to the space MoUs as much as any other: Agnikul and Hathor are young launch companies, and a proposed investment becomes a facility only after land allocation, clearances and financing close. What changed this week is concrete — a named land bank of 5,000 acres and two signed space-sector proposals. What has not yet changed is anything on the ground near Tirupati.

The summit also carried the government's P4 poverty initiative: Hero MotoCorp signed a P4 MoU for scholarships, and ITC signed on to support 100 villages, 15 of them as model villages, according to the summit reporting.
